messages:
Elena: Heads-up: RFC follow-up — propose we formalize a Quant Profile manifest schema (v1) that includes provenance, kernel ABI, and hardware constraints. Goal: make rollouts safer and make runtime quickly reject incompatible profiles.
Rajat: High level — sounds useful. What fields are you thinking?
Elena: Sketch below. Key ideas: profile_version, calibration_snapshot_id (immutable), kernel_abi (libkernels major.minor), hardware_constraints (min_compute_capability, supported_memory_formats), fallback_order, canary_required (bool), deprecation_window_days. Also a signed_provenance blob (gpg or sigstore link).
Mina: Love the provenance idea. We keep getting weird regressions because folks re-upload profiles with same name but different calibration. How will calibration_snapshot_id map to eval_store?
Elena: calibration_snapshot_id points to a snapshot in eval-store (immutable hash). CI will require that the snapshot exists and include a small playback manifest. Runtime can fetch minimal stats (baseline embeddings variance) for live SNR checks.
Tom: Kernel ABI field is critical. Different kernel implementations (tensor layout/kernels) produce subtle diffs. How strict is kernel_abi matching?
Elena: Proposal: runtime requires equal major version; minor can be compatible but must be flagged. Example: kernel_abi: "libkernels@2.1". If profile was built/tested against 2.1 and runtime has 3.0, runtime will either reject or require an explicit compatibility shim flag in manifest. That avoids silent mismatches.
Rajat: We also need a migration path when we change kernel internals. Suggest deprecation_window_days and a compatibility matrix artifact where model owners declare tested runtimes.
Elena: Agreed. Manifest snippet: 
```yaml
quant_profile_manifest_version: "1"
profile_name: "fp8-balanced-v1"
profile_version: "2026-03-01-rc1"
calibration_snapshot_id: "sha256:ab12..."
kernel_abi: "libkernels@2.1"
hardware_constraints:
  min_compute_capability: "8.0"
  supported_mem_formats: ["nvf16","pack16"]
fallback_order: ["int8-compatible","float32"]
canary_required: true
depracation_window_days: "90"  # days before forced retirement
signed_provenance: "https://artifacts.redwood/prov/ab12.sig"
```
Mina: Nice. A couple questions: 1) schema must include whether per-token mixing is allowed (we default to false). 2) enforce canary_required on any profile that changes calibration_snapshot_id.
Elena: Good catches. Add field: allow_per_token_mixing: false by default. And yes, CI lint will fail if calibration changed without canary block.
Tom: Runtime behavior: when loading a profile, runtime will check kernel_abi and hardware_constraints. If mismatch -> either refuse to load or mark it as "compatibility-risk" and only allow in shadow mode. We should prefer fail-fast.
Rajat: Operationally, for customer safety we should require a signed_provenance or CI artifact before any production deploy. Lint-bot should block PRs without it.
lint-bot: New lint rule proposal opened: quant-manifest-provenance-required. PR will fail CI if signed_provenance missing for production profiles.
Mina: How do we surface deprecation to customers? Add metadata to API that lists supported_profiles and deprecation_date per profile?
Elena: Yes. Console + /models endpoint should include profile metadata and deprecation_date. Also send scheduled notices to tenants using soon-to-deprecate profiles.
Tom: Testing: add matrix tests in CI that validate profile load under candidate kernel_abi versions (matrix runner with libkernels 2.0/2.1/3.0). Also a lightweight runtime check that computes sample deg_score on a canned prompt set on load to detect major mismatches.
Elena: Implementation plan: 1) finalize schema PR, 2) add linter rules + CI checks, 3) runtime check for kernel_abi & hardware constraints + shadow-only load mode, 4) console + API exposure, 5) announce out-of-band. I'll open PRs for (1) and (2) today.
Rajat: +1. Also add a required changelog entry in the manifest when profile_version increments explaining calibration changes.
Elena: Will do. Action items recorded: Elena -> PRs for schema + lints; Tom -> runtime compatibility + sample-load check; Mina -> eval-store snapshot API hookup; Rajat -> console metadata endpoint.
Mina: One more: add an opt-in header for customers to prefer cost-first routing (they accept slightly larger deg_score) vs quality-first routing. That interacts with fallback_order.
Elena: Good idea. Header example: X-Quant-Pref: cost|quality. We'll include in the spec.
Tom: Thx. This should cut down on accidental regressions from ABI drift.
Elena: Thanks team. I'll post PR links here when ready.
